newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics falls after Zilog projection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics falls after Zilog projection.

text.p: Shares of modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp fell on Thursday in heavy trading, pressured by rumors that some manufacturers were experiencing a decline in demand, securities analysts said.

The analysts said the rumors were sparked by Zilog Inc's projection late Wednesday that its third quarter earnings would be substantially lower than second quarter. Zilog provides chips for modems among other things.
"Some people are trying to make a connection between Zilog's disappointments and U.S. Robotics," said Eric Buck, an analyst for Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
Buck said U.S. Robotics' top-selling modem does not contain a Zilog chip.
"It is very possible that Zilog supplies some of U.S. Robotics' competitors, but the fact they're having problems reflects U.S. Robotics' strength, not problems in the industry," Buck said.
U.S. Robotics shares were down 2-9/16 at 47-1/8, after dropping to a low of the day of 46-1/2. More than 4.6 million shares had traded.
A U.S. Robotics spokeswoman said the company does not comment on the stock market, but added that the company had made no announcements.
Analysts said momentum investors were possibly pulling out of the stock, but U.S. Robotics' fundamentals had not changed.

"I think the modem business is still very strong.... We think the quarter is going very well," said Amar Senan, an analyst for Volpe, Welty & Co. "It presents a tremendous buying opportunity for investors looking for stable, robust growth."
